title: Sprintless experiment register - personal sheet
body:
Quick summary:
This is a compact single-sheet capture for ad-hoc experiments I run between bigger notebooks. Goal: keep a reproducible one-line record per trial (variant) so I can quickly aggregate p50/p95 + cost math later. Kept intentionally terse — meant for copy/paste into bigger reports.

Table (CSV):
trial_id,date,model,variant,quant,cache_mode,batch_size,seq_len,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_generated,cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,notes,result
T-20260301-01,2026-03-01,redwood-7b,v1,fp16,none,1,256,34,82,12000,0.42,baseline no cache,OK
T-20260301-02,2026-03-01,redwood-7b,v1,int8,kvcache,1,256,22,48,11800,0.21,kvcache hit ~70%,good
T-20260302-01,2026-03-02,llama2-13b,v2,int8,kvcache,4,128,58,142,50000,0.30,batching=4 improves throughput,regression on q-levels
T-20260303-01,2026-03-03,redwood-7b,v1,int8,kvcache,8,64,26,58,98000,0.08,high throughput steady,keep
T-20260304-01,2026-03-04,redwood-7b,v3,int8,kvcache+prefix,2,512,95,210,24000,0.35,prefix caching warm-up noisy,investigate
T-20260305-01,2026-03-05,redwood-7b,v3,int4,kvcache,1,128,28,66,15000,0.06,int4 artifacts on rare tokens,clip-trunc observed,needs eval

Notes to self and quick heuristics:
- Always record tokens_generated (estimate from total char length + tokenizer conversion). I frequently forget and it wrecks cost math.
- Cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: quick calc used current infra price sheet (see linked PR). Round to 2 decimals for fast comparisons.
- Use kvcache+prefix only when sequence overlap >30%: otherwise warm-up cost > savings.
- For experiments marked "regression" or "needs eval" copy trial_id into `project/evals/pending` in confluence.

Open questions / TODOs:
- T-20260302-01: quantify accuracy drop for int8 on long-tail tokens (sample 500 prompts from prod-redactions). Add pass/fail threshold.
- T-20260304-01: instrument prefix cache hit-rate per request (not just per batch). Raise a small telemetry PR (linked).
- T-20260305-01: run int4 with quant-awareness disabled in runtime to isolate kernel vs quantization noise.

Quick checklist before archiving a trial row:
- [ ] tokens_generated validated (tooling script run)
- [ ] seed & prompt set noted in external eval doc (link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] basic qualitative check (3 random responses)
- [ ] add result tag: OK | investigate | fail

Scratchpad (one-line notes):
- tried lowering kv eviction threshold -> small p50 improvement but p95 worse (maybe lock contention).
- batch=8 on 7b int8 yields best cost/token on short sequences (<=64). Document in cost-playbook.
- hypothesis: int4 noise concentrated in subword boundaries -> create token-boundary probe.

Copy/paste snippet for reports (one-line format):
"T-20260303-01 | redwood-7b int8 kvcache batch8 seq64 | p50=26ms p95=58ms | tokens=98k | $0.08/1k | status=OK"

End of sheet.
